subject: scorpion
reasoning:
I'm planning out a scorpion model for the SDK, sketching real-world proportions for the body and curled tail, and starting to design the skeleton hierarchy with a root body joint and spine chain.

For the legs, I'm working out four pairs using two-bone IK with hip and foot targets positioned for a natural stance, bending knees upward, and setting segment lengths so the reach works geometrically. I'm also planning the tail as a curling chain of segments ending in a stinger, and figuring out parent-child joint relationships for the whole rig.

For the pincers, I'm laying out shoulder-elbow-wrist arm chains per side, then adding a palm shape at the wrist plus a fixed curving finger spike and a hinged movable claw joint to form the pincer mechanism.

Now moving to the body, I'm planning to loft the mesosoma along the spine chain using a sweep with a width/flatness radius function per station.

Then I want to add tergite plate segments across the back, placing flattened boxes along the spine with ridges and paint stripes to break up the surface visually.

For the carapace, I'm thinking of using a scaled sphere part positioned at the front of the spine, then moving on to placing the eyes.

For the tail, I'm plotting out a curved path of points sweeping up and over the body toward a forward-pointing stinger, then chaining it from the rearmost spine joint with tapered, slightly bulging segments along the way.

I'm placing a telson bulb at the final tail joint and attaching a curved spike for the stinger, giving it a venomous barb look.

Defining joints for the mouthparts and head now, planning small chelicerae boxes as jaw joints parented under the front of the spine, plus a head joint at the carapace, before setting up the root joint and spine chain order.

For coloring, I'm picking a desert scorpion palette -- amber body, darker ridges, dark stinger, pale telson -- using a countershaded mottle pattern. Now I'm setting up leg joint chains per side, defining limb root points and bend directions for the limb function.

Working out foot target positions and leg lengths...

Attaching parent via nearest spine joint instead, then sweeping leg radii tapering from hip to foot, adding a small knee sphere for detail, and now laying out the pincer chain points from shoulder through elbow to wrist with tapered sweep radii and a palm center.

Still working out finger geometry...

Still placing body parts...

Still placing tergite segments...

Now I'm plotting the tail's curve with catmull points rising upward and curling, from the base near the body up through a stinger arc.

I'm setting up a chain of tail joints named "tail1" onward, sweeping the tail geometry and using a periodic paint function to alternate dark and amber bands for a segmented look, while tapering the radius slightly along its length.

Now I'm placing a telson bulb at the tail's end and shaping a curved stinger using a short bezier hook that dips and tapers to a point, anchored to the last tail bone.

I'm checking tail joint naming and tangent direction for smooth bending, then adding surface scatter detail—small granules sprinkled across the upper carapace—to give it texture.
